# Code vs Soul  
### Distinguishing AI-Generated Text from Human-Written Content Using Deep Learning

---

## Project Overview

**Code vs Soul** aims to classify whether a piece of text is generated by an AI model or written by a human. With the rise of generative language models, distinguishing between human creativity and machine output has become a crucial challenge. This project leverages natural language processing and deep learning to solve that binary classification task.

---

## Dataset

- **Source**: [AI vs Human Text Dataset – Kaggle](https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/shanegerami/ai-vs-human-text)
- **Description**: A balanced dataset containing labeled samples of both human-written and AI-generated text. The dataset captures a variety of text lengths, styles, and complexities for robust classification.

---

## Methodology

- **Data Preprocessing**:  
  - Text normalization (lowercasing, punctuation cleaning)  
  - Tokenization and removal of noise  

- **Feature Extraction**:  
  - Generated vector embeddings using **Word2Vec** to capture semantic meaning  

- **Model Development**:  
  - Built and trained two models:
    - Artificial Neural Network (ANN)
    - Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM)

- **Evaluation**:  
  - Measured performance using accuracy and visualized loss/accuracy curves

---

## Dataset Insights

| Metric               | Mean     | Range                   |
|----------------------|----------|-------------------------|
| Word Count           | ~393     | 0 – 1668 words          |
| Text Length          | ~2270    | 1 – 18,322 characters   |
| Average Word Length  | ~4.76    | 1 – 126 characters      |
| Punctuation Count    | ~48      | 0 – 388 marks           |
| Lexical Diversity    | ~0.51    | 0 – 1 (unique word ratio)|
